extraFacts.fact: NPSM is the straight (parallel) mechanical pipe thread of ASME B1.20.1; NST (also called NH) is the national standard hose coupling thread and GHT the garden hose thread, both in ASME B1.20.7. Straight threads seal on a gasket or washer, not on the thread.
extraFacts.source: ASME B1.20.1 Pipe Threads, General Purpose (Inch); ASME B1.20.7 Hose Coupling Screw Threads (Inch)

faqs.q: What are the Dixon Boss Female Adapters and what are they used for?
faqs.a: Dixon Boss Female Adapters are ground joint wing nut by female NPT adapters in plated iron or steel. The wing nut end joins a Boss ground joint coupling, and the female NPT end takes a male pipe thread. Six sizes run from 3/4" to 3" thread size.

faqs.q: How do the Dixon Boss female adapter part numbers GFAS6 to GFAS36 map to sizes?
faqs.a: The number after GFAS rises with the size: GFAS6 is 3/4", GFAS11 is 1", GFAS16 is 1-1/4", GFAS21 is 1-1/2", GFAS26 is 2" and GFAS36 is 3" female NPT thread. All six are listed as plated iron or steel.

faqs.q: What sizes and part numbers do the Dixon Boss Female Adapters cover?
faqs.a: The six part numbers are GFAS6, GFAS11, GFAS16, GFAS21, GFAS26 and GFAS36, covering female NPT threads of 3/4", 1", 1-1/4", 1-1/2", 2" and 3". Each part number is one size.

faqs.q: How do I pick a Dixon Boss female adapter for my pipe thread?
faqs.a: Pick the size of the male NPT pipe thread you are joining to: a 2" male thread needs the 2" female adapter, GFAS26. The Boss end and the NPT end are matched, so state the size of the ground joint coupling on the other side as well.

faqs.q: What pressure rating do the Dixon Boss Female Adapters have?
faqs.a: The Dixon Boss Female Adapters do not carry one pressure figure on their listing, because ratings vary by part number. Give us your working pressure and size and we will confirm the rating with the manufacturer before supply. The hose and its clamp or ferrule usually limit the joint before the fitting does.

faqs.q: What are the Dixon Boss female adapters made from?
faqs.a: The listing gives iron and steel, with a plated finish. Plated iron or steel suits air, water and general utility lines; the plating protects the surface but is not a stainless or chemical-resistant choice.

faqs.q: What does the Dixon Boss female adapter connect to?
faqs.a: Its ground joint wing nut end connects to a Boss ground joint half, and its female NPT end screws onto a male pipe thread. For the male version see [Dixon Boss male adapters](/p/dixon-boss-male-adapters), and for hose ends see [Boss holedall fittings](/p/dixon-boss-holedall-fittings).

faqs.q: How do I fit the Dixon Boss female adapter?
faqs.a: Seal the NPT end with thread sealant or tape and tighten it onto the pipe, then bring the ground joint seat together with the mating half and tighten the wing nut. Keep the seat clean, because dirt on the ground faces stops the joint sealing.

faqs.q: What thread standard does the Dixon Boss female adapter use?
faqs.a: The pipe end is NPT, a tapered pipe thread, so it seals with thread sealant or tape. The other end is a ground joint wing nut, which seals on the ground seat of the mating Boss coupling.

faqs.q: How do Dixon Boss female adapters differ from Boss male adapters?
faqs.a: The female adapter has female NPT threads and takes a male pipe end, while the [Boss male adapter](/p/dixon-boss-male-adapters) has a male NPT thread and screws into a female port. Both are listed in six sizes from 3/4" to 3".

faqs.a: The number after GMAS rises with the size: GMAS6 is 3/4", GMAS11 is 1", GMAS16 is 1-1/4", GMAS21 is 1-1/2", GMAS26 is 2" and GMAS36 is 3" male NPT thread, all in plated iron or steel.

faqs.q: What sizes and part numbers do the Dixon Boss Male Adapters cover?

faqs.q: Which Dixon Boss male adapter do I need for a given port?

faqs.a: Wrap or coat the male NPT thread with sealant and tighten it into the port, then bring the ground joint faces together with the wing nut. Keep both ground faces clean, because dirt on the seat is a common cause of leaks.

faqs.q: What thread does the Dixon Boss male adapter use?
faqs.a: The pipe end is a male NPT thread, which is tapered and seals with thread sealant or tape. The other end is a ground joint, which seals on the ground seat of the mating Boss half.

faqs.q: What are the Dixon Boss Holedall Fittings and what are they used for?
faqs.a: Dixon Boss Holedall Fittings are hose-end fittings in plated iron, steel or stainless steel, sized by body size from 3/4" to 3". Each part number covers one band of hose outside diameter, so the fitting grips the hose without a separate ferrule.

faqs.q: How do I choose between the P1, P2 and P3 Dixon Boss holedall part numbers?
faqs.a: The letters P1, P2 and P3 at the end of the part number step through the hose outside diameter bands for one body size. For the 3" body, GF111P1 fits 3-26/64 to 3-40/64 inch hose, GF111P2 fits 3-41/64 to 3-48/64 inch and GF111P3 fits 3-49/64 to 3-56/64 inch.

faqs.q: What sizes and part numbers do the Dixon Boss Holedall Fittings cover?
faqs.a: The 18 part numbers cover body sizes 3/4", 1", 1-1/2", 2" and 3". Each body size has several hose outside diameter bands, for example the 2" body covers 2-28/64 to 2-56/64 inch in three steps. Three part numbers beginning RGF are listed as hose couplings.

faqs.q: How do I find the right Dixon Boss holedall for my hose?
faqs.a: Measure the hose outside diameter and pick the part number whose band contains it. A hose of 1-35/64 inch outside diameter, for example, falls in the 1" body band of GF36P2, which covers 1-35/64 to 1-38/64 inch.

faqs.q: What pressure rating do the Dixon Boss Holedall Fittings have?
faqs.a: The Dixon Boss Holedall Fittings do not carry one pressure figure on their listing, because ratings vary by part number. Give us your working pressure and size and we will confirm the rating with the manufacturer before supply. The hose and its clamp or ferrule usually limit the joint before the fitting does.

faqs.q: What are Dixon Boss holedall fittings made from?
faqs.a: The listing gives plated iron, steel and stainless steel, so the choice follows the medium: plated iron or steel for general utility lines and stainless for more corrosive service. State the material you need when you enquire.

faqs.q: What does a Dixon Boss holedall fitting connect to?
faqs.a: The Boss end connects to another Boss half through the ground joint seat and wing nut, and the hose end clamps the hose. For the pipe adapters of the same Boss family see [Dixon Boss male adapters](/p/dixon-boss-male-adapters) and [female adapters](/p/dixon-boss-female-adapters).

faqs.q: How do I fit a Dixon Boss holedall to a hose?
faqs.a: Cut the hose square, push it fully onto the fitting stem and close the clamp over the band that matches its outside diameter. A hose outside the band for the part number will leak or pull off, so measure it before you order.

faqs.q: Which standard do the Dixon Boss Holedall Fittings follow?

faqs.q: What are the Dixon Female Hose Shank Adapters and what are they used for?
faqs.a: Dixon Female Hose Shank Adapters are quick-connect female couplers with a hose shank, in galvanized steel. They are Type B (and Type A in larger sizes) female cam and groove halves from 2" to 12" that connect hose to a male adapter.

faqs.q: How do I read the Dixon female hose shank adapter part numbers FC3103 to FC31012?
faqs.a: The FC31 codes are Type B female by hose shank in galvanized steel, and the digits after them give the size: FC3103 is 3", FC3106 is 6" and FC31012 is 12". Codes starting FC21 are Type A, shown for 10" and 12". ST suffixes such as FC3106ST60 mark the machined hose shank version.

faqs.q: What sizes and part numbers do the Dixon Female Hose Shank Adapters cover?
faqs.a: The 12 part numbers cover 2", 3", 4", 6", 8", 10" and 12" sizes in galvanized steel. Type B is the main version, Type A is listed in 10" and 12", and the ST codes are machined shank versions.

faqs.q: Which Dixon female hose shank adapter do I need for Type A or Type B?
faqs.a: Pick the type to match the male adapter you will join: Type A and Type B are different cam and groove styles. Then pick the size of the hose bore. The machined shank ST versions suit applications that need a machined hose tail.

faqs.q: What pressure rating do the Dixon Female Hose Shank Adapters have?
faqs.a: The Dixon Female Hose Shank Adapters do not carry one pressure figure on their listing, because ratings vary by part number. Give us your working pressure and size and we will confirm the rating with the manufacturer before supply. The hose and its clamp or ferrule usually limit the joint before the fitting does.

faqs.q: What are Dixon female hose shank adapters made from?

faqs.q: Do I need a nylon or a polypropylene Dixon hose shank?

faqs.q: What pressure rating do the Dixon Hose Shanks have?
faqs.a: The Dixon Hose Shanks do not carry one pressure figure on their listing, because ratings vary by part number. faqs.q: What does a Dixon hose shank screw into?
